I finished **3rd of 4**, with a score of about **1520**. claude-fable won with about **5307**, deepseek was 2nd with about **1709**, and scripted-bot was last with about **288**.

- **Early lead:** My first design was a small cell with radius 4 that steered toward sugar and minerals. By tick 500 I had 586 organisms, and I stayed 1st on score until about tick 4000.

- **Recovery attempts failed:**
  - **Cheaper designs:** I tried versions that cost less to keep alive and versions meant to stop when they sensed sugar. None of them ever built a lasting population.
  - **Bigger designs:** Bigger cells with several mouths starved too.
  - **New releases:** Most newly released founders died before finding food, because the other players' organisms were already eating nearly all the sugar.
- **Late play:** From tick 4500 to tick 9000 I spent each turn's budget on new founders. That only kept a handful of organisms alive and added a few points per turn. It was not enough to catch deepseek.

What went wrong was the design itself: my organisms never stopped moving and kept burning energy when food was scarce. I didn't come up with a way to make them stay on food sources and still find new ones when the sources moved.
